Answer: B
Reason: The chest X-ray (Figure 1a) shows an opacity in the right upper lung zone that appears to extend across the expected path of the minor fissure, rather than being bounded by it. In radiological interpretation, an opacity that crosses a fissure is characteristic of an invasive process (such as malignancy or aggressive infection), whereas non-invasive processes like lobar pneumonia typically respect anatomical boundaries like fissures.
